customer_updates.name: Naveen Mendan
customer_updates.text:
​I recently headed over to Ravindra Restaurant in Dahisar East for a traditional morning breakfast, and overall, it was a fantastic culinary experience. If you’re looking for authentic flavors to kickstart your day, this place definitely hits the mark.
​We decided to order a spread of classic items to get a real feel for the kitchen’s quality: tea, medu vada, masala uthappam, and the pineapple shera. To put it simply—the food was absolutely delicious. The medu vada was fried to perfection, offering that satisfying crisp exterior with a soft, fluffy center, and the sambar was well-spiced and flavorful. The masala uthappam was equally impressive, packed with fresh vegetables and cooked to just the right texture. The real highlight of the morning, however, was the pineapple shera. It was rich, fragrant, and perfectly balanced in sweetness—truly one of the best I’ve had in a while.
​While the kitchen is clearly doing a great job, the service side of the experience could definitely use some improvement. The restaurant was quite busy, and it felt like the staff was a bit overwhelmed, which led to noticeable delays in getting our order taken and getting the table cleared afterward. A bit more coordination and attentiveness from the service team would really elevate the visit.
​Despite the slow service, the high quality of the food makes Ravindra Restaurant a place I’d gladly visit again. They clearly have a strong handle on their recipes, and it’s a spot I’d recommend to anyone in the area looking for a quality breakfast. I’m hoping that things run a bit smoother on the service front next time, as it would make the entire experience five-star worthy.

featured_reviews.name: Naveen Mendan
featured_reviews.review_text:
​I recently dined at Hotel Ravindra in Dahisar (E), and it was a delightful experience for the palate.

​The Food Experience:
​Paneer Lajawab: This dish truly lived up to its name ("Lajawab" meaning matchless). The gravy was thick, well-textured, and had a perfect balance of tanginess and spice. The paneer cubes were fresh and soft, absorbing the flavors beautifully. It’s a must-order for vegetarians.
​Breads (Butter Naan & Kulcha): You can tell a lot about a kitchen by its tandoor work. The naan and kulchas were served piping hot, glistening with butter, and had that perfect slight crunch on the outside while remaining soft on the inside. The addition of kalonji seeds added a wonderful nutty aroma to every bite.
​Accompaniments: Even the simple additions like the fresh onion rings, lemon, and spicy pickle enhanced the meal significantly. We finished off with a hot tea which was the perfect palate cleanser.
​Ambiance & Service:
The restaurant has a warm, inviting atmosphere suitable for both families and quick dinners. The staff was courteous and the food arrived at our table surprisingly fast.
​The "Water" Hiccup:
The only slight downside to our evening was the coordination regarding drinking water. Despite the staff being polite, we had to request water multiple times before it finally reached the table. In a high-quality dining setup, basic table service like water should ideally be proactive.
​Final Verdict:

Despite the small delay with the water, the culinary experience was top-notch. The flavors are authentic, and the quality of ingredients is evident. I will definitely be returning to try more of their menu!

featured_reviews.review_text:
One fine evening while going for an evening walk, I found this place and couldn’t resist visiting. It looked like a small, cozy food joint serving mostly parathas, true to its name, Khaas Parathas. Since then, it has become my and my sister's go-to spot for quick snacks or even full-fledged meals. Though parathas are their specialty, the menu also features South Indian delicacies, Punjabi dishes, sweet treats, and an array of refreshing juices and beverages. The staff here are warm and friendly, and Mahesh, the owner, is polite and approachable.

The parathas are stuffed to perfection, loaded with flavor, and served hot. My all-time favorites are the Masala Pav and Cheese Pav Bhaji - both are mouthwateringly delicious and worth every bite. The vibrant yet peaceful ambience makes this place a hidden gem.

Quality - 5/5

Price - ₹500 for 2 people

featured_reviews.name: Shreyas Saddalgi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Malgudi: Great Vibes, Confused Kitchen & Extra Fees
Let’s be real—I wanted to love this place. Walking into Malgudi on SV Road, the vibe is immaculate. It sets you up for a cozy, authentic South Indian experience. But between the kitchen confusion and the final bill, it’s a bit of a rollercoaster.
Here is the unfiltered breakdown:
The Star of the Show
If you go here, do yourself a favor and order the Benne Masala Dosa. It was genuinely too good—crispy, buttery, and exactly what you hope for. The chutney pairing was also on point and very tasty.
The "What happened here?" Section
Unfortunately, the rest of the meal felt like an identity crisis.
• The Sambar Situation: This was weird. The sambar actually tasted different across different dishes. Consistency is key, guys—pick a lane!
• Portions & Options: The menu feels very limited, and the portion sizes are basically a tease. For the price, you expect to leave full, not looking for a snack on the way home.
• Overall Taste: Aside from the Benne Dosa, the general taste could really be improved. It feels like they are holding back flavor.
The Coffee Letdown
For a place with this vibe, you expect the coffee game to be strong. It wasn't.
• Coffee Mocktails: Hard pass. They just felt not worth the price tag.
• Filter Coffee: The ultimate test for a South Indian spot, and they failed it. It tasted average at best and definitely lacked that authentic "kick" you crave.
The Final Pinch
Just when you are questioning the portion sizes vs. the price, the bill arrives. They levy a 5% Service Charge.
Paying extra for "service" when the filter coffee is average and the sambar is inconsistent? That stings.
The Verdict
Go for the Benne Masala Dosa and the aesthetic, but lower your expectations for everything else. It’s a great place to sit, but be ready to pay a premium (plus 5%) for a mixed bag of flavors.

featured_reviews.name: ralph sequeira
featured_reviews.review_text:
Wanted to dine here for a long time, finally got the opportunity, so visited with my wife.  Good part is this is a wine and dine restaurant plus you have lot of the coastal and mangalorean and goan and chinese cusine available .

We tried a beer and multiple different starters.

The ambience is very good made for family and friends alike.
The owner plays some good 80s-90s Indian music which is not too loud so you can have a conversation .
The food is very good and the service is fast.
Surely to visit again to try out the dishes I didn't this time.

Only draw back is the pricing is a little on the expensive side, but even if you are price sensitive it is a one time try.
